title: The Necessity of Setting Temperature in LLM-as-a-Judge
abstract: arXiv:2603.28304v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used as automated judges, yet decoding temperature is often set by intuition rather than evidence. We run over one million large scale evaluations, multiple open-source models, prompting strategies, and judging paradigms to examine how temperature affects judge reliability. Low temperatures yield consistent outputs with few errors, especially in smaller models, while higher temperatures reduce consistency and increase errors. Yet consistency alone does not guarantee sound judgments: low temperatures can narrow the range of reasoning explored. We characterize judge behavior through four reasoning personas and find that temperature shifts their distributions in model-dependent ways, most visibly in ambiguous cases where competing answers are hard to distinguish. translated_title: 论LLM-as-a-Judge（大语言模型作为评判者）中设置温度的必要性
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被用作自动评判者，然而解码温度的设置通常基于直觉而非证据。我们进行了超过一百万次大规模评估，涵盖多个开源模型、提示策略和评判范式，以研究温度如何影响评判者的可靠性。低温能产生一致且错误较少的输出，在较小的模型中尤其明显；而较高的温度会降低一致性并增加错误。然而，仅凭一致性并不能保证判断的合理性：低温可能会缩小所探索的推理范围。我们通过四种推理人格来刻画评判者的行为，发现温度会以依赖于模型的方式改变这些人格的分布，在竞争答案难以区分的模糊案例中表现得最为明显。重复的高温采样能够揭示这种隐藏的不确定性，将其与多数投票相结合或使用高温度……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究通过超过一百万次大规模评估首次系统证明了LLM作为评判者时温度设置的必要性：低温虽能保证输出一致性但会缩小推理探索范围，而高温重复采样结合多数投票可揭示隐藏的不确定性。
en_tdlr: Through over one million large-scale evaluations, this study systematically demonstrates the necessity of setting temperature in LLM-as-a-Judge: low temperature ensures consistency but narrows reasoning exploration, while repeated high-temperature sampling combined with majority voting reveals hidden uncertainty.
